profile.intro: I am a DevOps engineer with an M.Sc. in Software Engineering and 2.5 years of research developing distributed prototypes at TU Berlin. I work with Linux, Docker, Kubernetes, Jenkins CI/CD, Terraform, Ansible and AWS, backed by a programming background in Java and Python. I care about reproducible benchmarks, clear technical documentation and infrastructure that teams can trust.

projects.title: Nine-stage Jenkins CI/CD pipeline
projects.summary: An end-to-end Jenkins pipeline for a rental-car application that connects Git, infrastructure provisioning, Docker image builds and deployment.
projects.details:
The pipeline turns every push into a reproducible delivery: the code is checked out, infrastructure is provisioned with Terraform, servers are configured with Ansible, the application is built into Docker images and pushed to a registry, and the new version is deployed.

Each stage is a separate, observable step, so a failure is easy to locate and the whole flow can be re-run from a clean state.
results: 9 automated stages from commit to deployment
Infrastructure and app delivered by one pipeline
Repeatable runs from a clean state

projects.title: Multi-tier AWS environment with Terraform
projects.summary: A highly available multi-tier web environment on AWS, provisioned with reusable Terraform modules and variables.
projects.details:
Traffic enters through Route 53 and an Application Load Balancer that spreads requests across EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group inside a dedicated VPC. Application data is stored in Amazon RDS and static assets in S3, with access controlled by IAM roles.

The whole environment is described as Terraform code with reusable modules and variables, so it can be created, changed and destroyed reproducibly.

projects.title: OptiFaaS — serverless benchmarking
projects.summary: Distributed prototypes and repeatable benchmarks for Function-as-a-Service and event-driven cloud architectures.
projects.details:
Within the OptiFaaS research project I developed distributed software prototypes in Java and deployed them on AWS Lambda and Google Cloud Functions, packaged with Docker on Linux.

I built repeatable benchmarks to evaluate scalability, concurrency and performance across distributed workloads, and documented implementations and results for an international research team.
results: Repeatable benchmark setup across two cloud providers
Scalability & concurrency evaluated on real workloads
Results documented for an international team

projects.title: HetEng — energy-efficient IoT clustering
projects.summary: An improved distributed, energy-efficient clustering scheme for heterogeneous IoT networks.
projects.details:
My master's thesis studied how heterogeneous clustering can reduce power consumption in IoT networks. Nodes are organised into clusters whose heads aggregate data and forward it to the base station, so fewer nodes spend energy on long-distance transmission.

The work was published at the 2021 IEEE International Conference on Industry 4.0, Artificial Intelligence and Communications Technology.
results: Lower energy use through heterogeneous clustering

projects.title: Remote home monitoring system

projects.details: My bachelor's thesis covered the design and implementation of a remote home monitoring system: sensors in the home report their state to a central service, which users can check remotely.
